gloss: beef tongue (esp. grilled, as a Sendai specialty)

definitions.explanation: Sliced beef tongue, usually salted and grilled over charcoal. It is the signature dish of {仙台|せんだい} and a standard item at yakiniku restaurants nationwide.

examples.japanese: {牛|ぎゅう}タンを{注文|ちゅうもん}した。
{仙台|せんだい}に{行|い}ったら{牛|ぎゅう}タン{定食|ていしょく}は{外|はず}せない。
examples.english: If you go to Sendai, the beef tongue set meal is a must.

examples.japanese: {厚切|あつぎ}りの{牛|ぎゅう}タンを{炭火|すみび}で{焼|や}いて、レモンをしぼって{食|た}べた。
examples.english: We grilled thick-cut beef tongue over charcoal and ate it with a squeeze of lemon.

notes:
Written {牛|ぎゅう}タン, with タン from English "tongue." The all-kanji spelling {牛舌|ぎゅうぜつ} exists but is rare on menus.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {牛|ぎゅう}タン{定食|ていしょく}: a beef tongue set meal (with barley rice and oxtail soup)
- {厚切|あつぎ}り{牛|ぎゅう}タン: thick-cut beef tongue
- {牛|ぎゅう}タン{塩|しお}: salt-seasoned beef tongue, the standard preparation
- {仙台|せんだい}{名物|めいぶつ}の{牛|ぎゅう}タン: Sendai's famous beef tongue

CULTURAL NOTE:
Grilled beef tongue was developed by a Sendai restaurateur after the war and is now the city's best-known souvenir food, sold vacuum-packed at {仙台|せんだい}{駅|えき}. Ordering it as a set with {麦|むぎ}ごはん and テールスープ is the local convention.
